name: Permute Digits
description: You are given two positive integer numbers a and b . Permute (change order) of the digits of a to construct maximal number not exceeding b . No number in input and/or output can start with the digit 0 . It is allowed to leave a as it is.
input_specification: The first line contains integer a ( 1 ≤ a ≤ 10 18 ). The second line contains integer b ( 1 ≤ b ≤ 10 18 ). Numbers don't have leading zeroes. It is guaranteed that answer exists.
output_specification: Print the maximum possible number that is a permutation of digits of a and is not greater than b . The answer can't have any leading zeroes. It is guaranteed that the answer exists. The number in the output should have exactly the same length as number a . It should be a permutation of digits of a .
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 915C — Permute Digits [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
